# Script

- Inherits [`BaseScript`](basescript.md)
- Created with `Instance.new("Script")`

Luau code that runs. A script runs while it is enabled, is in the world and not under a storage service, and its side (server or client) runs on this machine.

Where a script is parented decides where it runs. A script under `ServerScriptService` or `GlobalScriptService.Server` runs only on the machine that is the authority. A script under `ClientScriptService` or `GlobalScriptService.Client` runs only on a machine with a player, never on a dedicated server. Anywhere else, `RunContext` decides.

In the editor, scripts start when you press Play. Opening a project loads every script, so you can see and edit its `Source`, but starts none of them. Stop shuts the script VM down, so every Play starts from the same state. Outside the editor, scripts start when the game starts.

This page lists the members this class declares. Inherited members are
listed on the page of the class that declares them.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | read/write | Whether this script runs. A script that is disabled when the game starts never starts.<br><br>Setting it to true starts the script from the top of its code, even if it has run before. Setting it to false stops the script's threads from being resumed: deferred and delayed tasks and signal handlers no longer run, and a thread that is running continues until it next yields. The change takes effect at the next deferred update.<br><br>Disabling a script does not disconnect its connections and does not undo or remove anything it made. Disconnect them yourself if you need to. Scripts enabled in the same tick start in tree order. |
| `RunContext` | `Enum.RunContext` | `Enum.RunContext.Shared` | read-only to scripts; the editor writes it | Which side runs this script when it is outside the script services: `Server` on the authority, `Client` on a machine with a player, or `Shared` on both. A `Shared` script runs once per machine, so a solo game runs it once. Inside `ServerScriptService`, `ClientScriptService` and the `Server` and `Client` folders of `GlobalScriptService`, the service decides, and moving a script into one sets this property to that side.<br><br>An exported game leaves out the code of every script whose side never runs on that machine. The instance stays, with an empty `Source`, so a stamp can hold a server half and a client half.<br><br>Only the editor can set it; a running script can only read it. |
